To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-

ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

macros and a program to process LaTeX documents, and because the plain

arating presentation from content, so that authors can focus on the content of
what they are writing without attending simultaneously to its visual appear-
ance. In preparing a LaTeX document, the author specifies the logical structure
using simple, familiar concepts such as chapter, section, table, figure, etc., and

a result, it encourages the separation of the layout from the content — while
still allowing manual typesetting adjustments whenever needed. This concept
is similar to the mechanism by which many word processors allow styles to be
defined globally for an entire document, or the use of Cascading Style Sheets in
styling HyperText Markup Language (HTML) documents.
The LaTeX system is a markup language that handles typesetting and ren-
dering,[14] and can be arbitrarily extended by using the underlying macro lan-
guage to develop custom macros such as new environments and commands. Such
macros are often collected into packages, which could then be made available
to address some specific typesetting needs such as the formatting of complex
mathematical expressions or graphics (e.g., the use of the align environment
provided by the amsmath package to produce aligned equations).

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-

According to the document, there are five French mother sauces, and the document provides instructions for making four of them. Here are the instructions:

1. Béchamel (White Sauce)
(a) Make a white roux:
i. Melt butter in a saucepan.
ii. Add equal parts flour.
iii. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
(b) Gradually whisk in hot milk.
(c) Simmer until thickened.
(d) Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
2. Velouté:
(a) Make a blonde roux:
i. Melt butter in a saucepan.
ii. Add equal parts flour.
iii. Cook until lightly browned, stirring constantly.
(b) Gradually whisk in hot stock (chicken, veal, or fish).
(c) Simmer and reduce.
(d) Season to taste.
3. Espagnole (Brown Sauce)
(a) Make a brown roux:
i. Melt butter in a saucepan.
ii. Add equal parts flour.
iii. Cook until dark brown, about 8-10 minutes.
(b) Add mirepoix and tomato purée.
(c) Gradually incorporate hot brown stock.
(d) Simmer and reduce.
(e) Strain before using.
4. Hollandaise:
(a) Prepare clarified butter.
(b) Create the reduction:
i. Combine vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots.
ii. Reduce by half.
iii. Strain and cool slightly.
(c) Whisk egg yolks with reduction.
(d) Cook over double boiler until thickened.
(e) Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter.
(f) Season with lemon juice and cayenne.

The fifth French mother sauce, Tomato Sauce, is not provided in the document.

case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate

keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-

each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

According to the information provided in the document "procedures2.pdf", to make Hollandaise sauce, follow these steps:

1. Prepare clarified butter:
   a. Melt butter in a saucepan.
   b. Let it sit for a few minutes to allow the milk solids to settle at the bottom.
   c. Carefully pour the clear yellow butter from the top into a separate container, leaving the milk solids behind.

2. Create the reduction:
   a. Combine vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots in a saucepan.
   b. Reduce by half.
   c. Strain and cool slightly.

3. Whisk egg yolks with reduction:
   a. Whisk egg yolks in a heatproof bowl.
   b. Gradually whisk in the cooled reduction.

4. Cook over double boiler until thickened:
   a. Place the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water, ensuring the bottom of the bowl does not touch the water.
   b. Whisk the mixture constantly until it thickens and coats the back of a spoon.

5. Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter:
   a. Drizzle in the warm clarified butter, a few drops at a time, while continuously whisking the sauce.
   b. Be careful not to add the butter too quickly, as it may cause the sauce to break.

6. Season with lemon juice and cayenne:
   a. Add lemon juice and cayenne to taste.
   b. Whisk until well combined.

7. Serve immediately. If not serving immediately, keep the sauce warm over the double boiler, stirring occasionally to prevent it from thickening too much.

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.
To build H2O with Hadoop support yourself, first install sphinx for python:
pip install sphinx Then start the build by entering the following from the top-
level h2o-3 directory:
./gradlew build -x test; ./gradlew dist;
./gradlew build -x test; ./gradlew dist; Adding support for a new version of
Hadoop In the h2o-hadoop directory, each Hadoop version has a build directory
for the driver and an assembly directory for the fatjar.
You need to:
Add a new driver directory and assembly directory (each with a build.gradle
file) in h2o-hadoop Add these new projects to h2o-3/settings.gradle Add the new
Hadoop version to the list in h2o-dist/buildinfo.json Secure user impersonation
Hadoop supports secure user impersonation through its Java API. A kerberos-
authenticated user can be allowed to proxy any username that meets specified
criteria entered in the NameNode’s core-site.xml file. This impersonation only
applies to interactions with the Hadoop API or the APIs of Hadoop-related
services that support it (this is not the same as switching to that user on the
machine of origin).

LaTeX can be used as a standalone document preparation system, or as an
intermediate format. In the latter role, for example, it is sometimes used as part

The typesetting system offers programmable desktop publishing features and
extensive facilities for automating most aspects of typesetting and desktop pub-
lishing, including numbering and cross-referencing of tables and figures, chapter
and section headings, graphics, page layout, indexing and bibliographies.
Like TeX, LaTeX started as a writing tool for mathematicians and computer
scientists, but even from early in its development, it has also been taken up by
scholars who needed to write documents that include complex math expressions
or non-Latin scripts,[7][8] such as Arabic, Devanagari and Chinese.[9]
LaTeX is intended to provide a high-level, descriptive markup language to
utilize TeX more easily. TeX handles the document layout, while LaTeX handles
the content side for document processing. LaTeX comprises a collection of TeX
macros and a program to process LaTeX documents, and because the plain
TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made
commands for formatting and layout requirements such as chapter headings,
footnotes, cross-references and bibliographies.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

1. Béchamel (White Sauce):
	* Make a white roux by melting butter in a saucepan and adding equal parts flour, cooking for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
	* Gradually whisk in hot milk.
	* Simmer until thickened.
	* Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
2. Velouté:
	* Make a blonde roux by melting butter in a saucepan and adding equal parts flour, cooking for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.

	* Simmer until thickened.
	* Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
3. Espagnole (Brown Sauce):
	* Make a brown roux by melting butter in a saucepan and adding equal parts flour, cooking until dark brown, about 8-10 minutes.

	* Gradually incorporate hot brown stock.
	* Simmer and reduce.
	* Strain before using.

	* Prepare clarified butter.

	* Sweat aromatics by cooking onions, carrots, and celery, and adding garlic and herbs.
	* Add tomatoes and stock.

to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

do not need the smalldata directory.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

Typesetting system LaTeX attempts to follow the design philosophy of sep-
arating presentation from content, so that authors can focus on the content of
what they are writing without attending simultaneously to its visual appear-
ance. In preparing a LaTeX document, the author specifies the logical structure
using simple, familiar concepts such as chapter, section, table, figure, etc., and
lets the LaTeX system handle the formatting and layout of these structures. As
2
a result, it encourages the separation of the layout from the content — while
still allowing manual typesetting adjustments whenever needed. This concept
is similar to the mechanism by which many word processors allow styles to be
defined globally for an entire document, or the use of Cascading Style Sheets in
styling HyperText Markup Language (HTML) documents.
The LaTeX system is a markup language that handles typesetting and ren-
dering,[14] and can be arbitrarily extended by using the underlying macro lan-
guage to develop custom macros such as new environments and commands. Such
macros are often collected into packages, which could then be made available
to address some specific typesetting needs such as the formatting of complex
mathematical expressions or graphics (e.g., the use of the align environment
provided by the amsmath package to produce aligned equations).

typesetting program for formatting its output, and is itself written in the TeX
macro language.
LaTeX can be used as a standalone document preparation system, or as an
intermediate format. In the latter role, for example, it is sometimes used as part
of a pipeline for translating DocBook and other XML-based formats for PDF.
The typesetting system offers programmable desktop publishing features and
extensive facilities for automating most aspects of typesetting and desktop pub-
lishing, including numbering and cross-referencing of tables and figures, chapter
and section headings, graphics, page layout, indexing and bibliographies.
Like TeX, LaTeX started as a writing tool for mathematicians and computer
scientists, but even from early in its development, it has also been taken up by
scholars who needed to write documents that include complex math expressions
or non-Latin scripts,[7][8] such as Arabic, Devanagari and Chinese.[9]
LaTeX is intended to provide a high-level, descriptive markup language to
utilize TeX more easily. TeX handles the document layout, while LaTeX handles
the content side for document processing. LaTeX comprises a collection of TeX
macros and a program to process LaTeX documents, and because the plain
TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made
commands for formatting and layout requirements such as chapter headings,
footnotes, cross-references and bibliographies.

ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-

which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-

ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

History LaTeX was created in the early 1980s by Leslie Lamport when he
was working at Stanford Research Institute (SRI). He needed to write TeX
macros for his own use and thought that with a little extra effort, he could
make a general package usable by others. Peter Gordon, an editor at Addison-
Wesley, convinced him to write a LaTeX user’s manual for publication (Lamport
was initially skeptical that anyone would pay money for it);[13] it came out
in 1986[3] and sold hundreds of thousands of copies.[13] Meanwhile, Lamport
released versions of his LaTeX macros in 1984 and 1985. On 21 August 1989, at

maintenance and development of LaTeX to Frank Mittelbach. Frank Mittelbach,

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

History LaTeX was created in the early 1980s by Leslie Lamport when he
was working at Stanford Research Institute (SRI). He needed to write TeX
macros for his own use and thought that with a little extra effort, he could
make a general package usable by others. Peter Gordon, an editor at Addison-

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

Typesetting system LaTeX attempts to follow the design philosophy of sep-
arating presentation from content, so that authors can focus on the content of
what they are writing without attending simultaneously to its visual appear-
ance. In preparing a LaTeX document, the author specifies the logical structure
using simple, familiar concepts such as chapter, section, table, figure, etc., and
lets the LaTeX system handle the formatting and layout of these structures. As
2
a result, it encourages the separation of the layout from the content — while
still allowing manual typesetting adjustments whenever needed. This concept
is similar to the mechanism by which many word processors allow styles to be
defined globally for an entire document, or the use of Cascading Style Sheets in
styling HyperText Markup Language (HTML) documents.
The LaTeX system is a markup language that handles typesetting and ren-
dering,[14] and can be arbitrarily extended by using the underlying macro lan-
guage to develop custom macros such as new environments and commands. Such
macros are often collected into packages, which could then be made available
to address some specific typesetting needs such as the formatting of complex
mathematical expressions or graphics (e.g., the use of the align environment
provided by the amsmath package to produce aligned equations).

1. Prepare the roux: Melt butter in a saucepan and add equal parts of flour. Cook the mixture until it turns a dark brown color, which usually takes about 8-10 minutes.

2. Add the mirepoix: Add the chopped onions, carrots, and celery to the saucepan and cook until they become translucent.

3. Add the tomato purée: Add the tomato purée to the saucepan and cook for a few minutes to release its flavors.

4. Add the brown stock: Gradually add the brown stock to the saucepan, stirring constantly to prevent lumps from forming. Reduce the heat and let the sauce simmer until it thickens.

5. Strain the sauce: Once the sauce has thickened, strain it through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any solids or impurities.

6. Season the sauce: Taste the espagnole sauce and season it with salt and pepper to your preference.

7. Serve the sauce: Espagnole sauce can be used as a base for various dishes, such as beef bourguignon or veal demi-glace.

Remember to adjust the ingredients and cooking time based on your personal taste and the specific recipe you are following.

to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make

Typesetting system LaTeX attempts to follow the design philosophy of sep-
arating presentation from content, so that authors can focus on the content of
what they are writing without attending simultaneously to its visual appear-
ance. In preparing a LaTeX document, the author specifies the logical structure
using simple, familiar concepts such as chapter, section, table, figure, etc., and
lets the LaTeX system handle the formatting and layout of these structures. As
2
a result, it encourages the separation of the layout from the content — while
still allowing manual typesetting adjustments whenever needed. This concept
is similar to the mechanism by which many word processors allow styles to be
defined globally for an entire document, or the use of Cascading Style Sheets in
styling HyperText Markup Language (HTML) documents.
The LaTeX system is a markup language that handles typesetting and ren-
dering,[14] and can be arbitrarily extended by using the underlying macro lan-
guage to develop custom macros such as new environments and commands. Such
macros are often collected into packages, which could then be made available
to address some specific typesetting needs such as the formatting of complex
mathematical expressions or graphics (e.g., the use of the align environment
provided by the amsmath package to produce aligned equations).

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

How to build h2o-3?
Getting started with H2O development requires JDK 1.8+, Node.js, Gradle,
Python and R. We use the Gradle wrapper (called gradlew) to ensure up-to-date
local versions of Gradle and other dependencies are installed in your develop-
ment directory.
4.1. Before building Building h2o requires a properly set up R environment
with required packages and Python environment with the following packages:
grip tabulate requests wheel To install these packages you can use pip or
conda. If you have troubles installing these packages on Windows, please follow
section Setup on Windows of this guide.
(Note: It is recommended to use some virtual environment such as Vir-
tualEnv, to install all packages. )
4.2. Building from the command line (Quick Start) To build H2O from the
repository, perform the following steps.

Recipe 1: Clone fresh, build, skip tests, and run H2O
4.1
Build H2O
git clone https://github.com/h2oai/h2o-3.git cd h2o-3 ./gradlew build -x test
You may encounter problems: e.g. npm missing. Install it: brew install npm
4.2
Start H2O
java -jar build/h2o.jar
Point browser to http://localhost:54321
Recipe 2: Clone fresh, build, and run tests (requires a working install of R)
git clone https://github.com/h2oai/h2o-3.git cd h2o-3 ./gradlew syncSmalldata
./gradlew syncRPackages ./gradlew build Notes:
Running tests starts five test JVMs that form an H2O cluster and requires
at least 8GB of RAM (preferably 16GB of RAM). Notes We recommend using
./gradlew clean after each git pull.
Skip tests by adding -x test at the end the gradle build command line.
Tests typically run for 7-10 minutes on a Macbook Pro laptop with 4 CPUs (8
hyperthreads) and 16 GB of RAM.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made
commands for formatting and layout requirements such as chapter headings,
footnotes, cross-references and bibliographies.

According to the provided document, to make Hollandaise sauce, follow these steps:

1. Prepare clarified butter: Melt butter in a saucepan over low heat. Skim off the foam that rises to the surface. Once the butter is clear, remove it from heat and let it cool slightly.

2. Create the reduction: Combine vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots in a small saucepan. Reduce by half over medium heat. Strain and cool slightly.

3. Whisk egg yolks with reduction: In a heatproof bowl, whisk egg yolks. Gradually add the cooled reduction while continuing to whisk.

4. Cook over double boiler: Place the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water, making sure the bottom of the bowl does not touch the water. Cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens and coats the back of a spoon.

5. Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter: Remove the bowl from the heat. Gradually add the warm clarified butter, a few drops at a time, while continuously whisking.

6. Season with lemon juice and cayenne: Stir in lemon juice and cayenne to taste. If the sauce becomes too thick, thin it with a little warm water.

7. Serve immediately: Use the Hollandaise sauce as a topping for eggs Benedict, asparagus, or other dishes.

1. Béchamel (White Sauce)
   a. Make a white roux:
      i. Melt butter in a saucepan.
      ii. Add equal parts flour.
      iii. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
   b. Gradually whisk in hot milk.

   a. Make a blonde roux:
      i. Melt butter in a saucepan.

   c. Simmer and reduce.

   a. Prepare clarified butter.

      i. Combine vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots.

      iii. Strain and cool slightly.
   c. Whisk egg yolks with reduction.
   d. Cook over double boiler until thickened.
   e. Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

### Beef Wellington Recipe

#### Ingredients:
- Beef tenderloin
- Salt and pepper
- Mushrooms
- Shallots
- Garlic
- Herbs (such as thyme or parsley)
- Puff pastry
- Egg wash
- Prosciutto slices (optional)
- Duxelles (a mixture of finely chopped mushrooms, shallots, and herbs)

#### Instructions:

1. **Prepare the Beef Tenderloin:**
   - Season the beef with salt and pepper.
   - Sear all sides in a hot pan until browned.
   - Let rest and cool completely.

2. **Make the Mushroom Duxelles:**
   - Finely chop mushrooms, shallots, and garlic.
   - Sauté until moisture evaporates.
   - Season with herbs and let cool.

3. **Prepare the Prosciutto Wrapping (optional):**
   - Lay out plastic wrap.
   - Arrange prosciutto slices in a rectangle.
   - Spread duxelles over prosciutto.
   - Place cooled beef in the center.
   - Roll tightly using plastic wrap.
   - Chill for 30 minutes.

4. **Wrap in Puff Pastry:**
   - Roll out puff pastry.
   - Unwrap beef from plastic.
   - Place beef in the center of the pastry.
   - Fold pastry around beef.
   - Seal edges with egg wash.
   - Score decorative pattern on top.

5. **Bake:**
   - Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
   - Brush pastry with egg wash.
   - Bake for 40-45 minutes until golden.
   - Let rest for 10 minutes before serving.

#### Serving:
- Serve with your choice of sides and garnishes.

This recipe provides a step-by-step guide to creating a delicious Beef Wellington, from preparing the beef to baking the pastry-wrapped dish. Enjoy!

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

### Rendang (Spiced Meat Stew)

#### Ingredients:
- Shallots
- Garlic
- Ginger
- Galangal
- Turmeric
- Chilies
- Lemongrass
- Ground spices (such as coriander, cumin, cloves, nutmeg, cinnamon, star anise, cardamom)
- Meat (typically beef)
- Coconut milk
- Kaffir lime leaves

#### Instructions:

1. **Prepare Spice Paste:**
   - Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, turmeric, chilies, and lemongrass.
   - Add ground spices and mix well.

2. **Cook the Base:**
   - Sauté the spice paste in a pan until fragrant.
   - Add the meat (typically beef) and cook until slightly browned.
   - Pour in coconut milk and add kaffir lime leaves.

3. **Slow Cook:**
   - Simmer the mixture on low heat.
   - Stir occasionally.
   - Cook until the liquid evaporates and the meat darkens.

4. **Serve:**
   - Rendang is typically served with steamed rice or other accompaniments.

This recipe involves slow cooking the meat in a rich, spicy coconut milk sauce until the liquid has evaporated and the meat is tender and flavorful.

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.
To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

According to the information provided in the document, here are the steps to make hollandaise sauce:

1. Prepare clarified butter: Melt unsalted butter in a saucepan over low heat and skim off the foam that rises to the top. Pour the clear, yellow butter into a bowl, leaving behind the milky solids at the bottom of the pan.
2. Create the reduction: Combine white wine vinegar, black peppercorns, and minced shallots in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and reduce by half. Strain the mixture through a fine-mesh sieve into a small bowl and let it cool slightly.
3. Whisk egg yolks with reduction: In a medium heatproof bowl, whisk together egg yolks and the cooled reduction.
4. Cook over double boiler: Place the bowl over a saucepan of simmering water, making sure the bottom of the bowl does not touch the water. Whisk the egg yolk mixture constantly until it thickens and becomes pale yellow, about 3-5 minutes.
5. Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter: Gradually add the warm clarified butter to the egg yolk mixture, whisking constantly. If the sauce becomes too thick, add a few drops of warm water.
6. Season with lemon juice and cayenne: Stir in fresh lemon juice and a pinch of cayenne pepper to taste. Serve immediately.

Note: Hollandaise sauce can easily curdle if it becomes too hot or if it is not whisked constantly. If the sauce does curdle, you can try to save it by whisking in a few drops of cold water or by blending it in a blender.

LaTeX is widely used in academia for the communication and publication of
scientific documents and technical note-taking in many fields, owing partially
to its support for complex mathematical notation.[4][5] It also has a prominent
role in the preparation and publication of books and articles that contain com-
plex multilingual materials, such as Arabic and Greek.[6] LaTeX uses the TeX
1

typesetting program for formatting its output, and is itself written in the TeX
macro language.
LaTeX can be used as a standalone document preparation system, or as an
intermediate format. In the latter role, for example, it is sometimes used as part
of a pipeline for translating DocBook and other XML-based formats for PDF.
The typesetting system offers programmable desktop publishing features and
extensive facilities for automating most aspects of typesetting and desktop pub-
lishing, including numbering and cross-referencing of tables and figures, chapter
and section headings, graphics, page layout, indexing and bibliographies.
Like TeX, LaTeX started as a writing tool for mathematicians and computer
scientists, but even from early in its development, it has also been taken up by
scholars who needed to write documents that include complex math expressions
or non-Latin scripts,[7][8] such as Arabic, Devanagari and Chinese.[9]
LaTeX is intended to provide a high-level, descriptive markup language to
utilize TeX more easily. TeX handles the document layout, while LaTeX handles
the content side for document processing. LaTeX comprises a collection of TeX
macros and a program to process LaTeX documents, and because the plain
TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made
commands for formatting and layout requirements such as chapter headings,
footnotes, cross-references and bibliographies.

LaTeX3 has since been
cancelled with features intended for that version being back-ported to LaTeX2e
since 2018.[11]
Typesetting system LaTeX attempts to follow the design philosophy of sep-
arating presentation from content, so that authors can focus on the content of
what they are writing without attending simultaneously to its visual appear-
ance. In preparing a LaTeX document, the author specifies the logical structure
using simple, familiar concepts such as chapter, section, table, figure, etc., and
lets the LaTeX system handle the formatting and layout of these structures. As
2
a result, it encourages the separation of the layout from the content — while
still allowing manual typesetting adjustments whenever needed. This concept
is similar to the mechanism by which many word processors allow styles to be
defined globally for an entire document, or the use of Cascading Style Sheets in
styling HyperText Markup Language (HTML) documents.
The LaTeX system is a markup language that handles typesetting and ren-
dering,[14] and can be arbitrarily extended by using the underlying macro lan-
guage to develop custom macros such as new environments and commands. Such
macros are often collected into packages, which could then be made available
to address some specific typesetting needs such as the formatting of complex
mathematical expressions or graphics (e.g., the use of the align environment
provided by the amsmath package to produce aligned equations).

Typesetting system LaTeX attempts to follow the design philosophy of sep-
arating presentation from content, so that authors can focus on the content of
what they are writing without attending simultaneously to its visual appear-
ance. In preparing a LaTeX document, the author specifies the logical structure
using simple, familiar concepts such as chapter, section, table, figure, etc., and
lets the LaTeX system handle the formatting and layout of these structures. As
2
a result, it encourages the separation of the layout from the content — while
still allowing manual typesetting adjustments whenever needed. This concept
is similar to the mechanism by which many word processors allow styles to be
defined globally for an entire document, or the use of Cascading Style Sheets in
styling HyperText Markup Language (HTML) documents.
The LaTeX system is a markup language that handles typesetting and ren-
dering,[14] and can be arbitrarily extended by using the underlying macro lan-
guage to develop custom macros such as new environments and commands. Such
macros are often collected into packages, which could then be made available
to address some specific typesetting needs such as the formatting of complex
mathematical expressions or graphics (e.g., the use of the align environment
provided by the amsmath package to produce aligned equations).

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

Typesetting system LaTeX attempts to follow the design philosophy of sep-
arating presentation from content, so that authors can focus on the content of
what they are writing without attending simultaneously to its visual appear-
ance. In preparing a LaTeX document, the author specifies the logical structure
using simple, familiar concepts such as chapter, section, table, figure, etc., and
lets the LaTeX system handle the formatting and layout of these structures. As
2
a result, it encourages the separation of the layout from the content — while
still allowing manual typesetting adjustments whenever needed. This concept
is similar to the mechanism by which many word processors allow styles to be
defined globally for an entire document, or the use of Cascading Style Sheets in
styling HyperText Markup Language (HTML) documents.
The LaTeX system is a markup language that handles typesetting and ren-
dering,[14] and can be arbitrarily extended by using the underlying macro lan-
guage to develop custom macros such as new environments and commands. Such
macros are often collected into packages, which could then be made available
to address some specific typesetting needs such as the formatting of complex
mathematical expressions or graphics (e.g., the use of the align environment
provided by the amsmath package to produce aligned equations).

ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-

to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

According to the information provided in the documents, to make Hollandaise sauce, follow these steps:

1. **Prepare clarified butter**:
   - Melt butter and separate the clear liquid from the milk solids.

2. **Create the reduction**:
   - Combine vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots in a saucepan.
   - Reduce the mixture by half.
   - Strain the reduction to remove solids and cool it slightly.

3. **Whisk egg yolks with reduction**:
   - In a bowl, whisk egg yolks together with the cooled reduction.

4. **Cook the mixture**:
   - Place the bowl over a double boiler (a bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water).
   - Whisk the mixture continuously until it thickens.

5. **Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter**:
   - Gradually add the warm clarified butter to the egg yolk mixture while continuing to whisk.
   - This will create an emulsion, thickening the sauce.

6. **Season the sauce**:
   - Add lemon juice and a pinch of cayenne pepper to taste.
   - Mix well to ensure the seasoning is evenly distributed.

By following these steps, you will create a classic Hollandaise sauce.

According to the information provided, here are the recipes for the French mother sauces:

1. **Béchamel (White Sauce)**
   - (a) Make a white roux:
     - i. Melt butter in a saucepan.
     - ii. Add equal parts flour.
     - iii. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly.
   - (b) Gradually whisk in hot milk.
   - (c) Simmer until thickened.
   - (d) Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

2. **Velouté**
   - (a) Make a blonde roux:
     - i. Melt butter in a saucepan.
     - ii. Add equal parts flour.
     - iii. Cook for a few minutes, stirring constantly.
   - (b) Gradually whisk in hot white stock (chicken, veal, or fish).
   - (c) Simmer until thickened.
   - (d) Season to taste.

3. **Espagnole (Brown Sauce)**
   - (a) Make a brown roux:
     - i. Melt butter in a saucepan.
     - ii. Add equal parts flour.
     - iii. Cook until dark brown, about 8-10 minutes.
   - (b) Add mirepoix and tomato purée.
   - (c) Gradually incorporate hot brown stock.
   - (d) Simmer and reduce.
   - (e) Strain before using.

4. **Hollandaise**
   - (a) Prepare clarified butter.
   - (b) Create the reduction:
     - i. Combine vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots.
     - ii. Reduce by half.
     - iii. Strain and cool slightly.
   - (c) Whisk egg yolks with reduction.
   - (d) Cook over a double boiler until thickened.
   - (e) Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter.
   - (f) Season with lemon juice and cayenne.

5. **Tomato Sauce**
   - (a) Sweat aromatics:
     - i. Cook onions, carrots, and celery.
     - ii. Add garlic and herbs.
   - (b) Add tomatoes and stock.
   - (c) Simmer until reduced and thickened.
   - (d) Strain if desired.
   - (e) Season to taste.

These recipes provide a foundation for creating the classic French mother sauces.

lets the LaTeX system handle the formatting and layout of these structures. As

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)

Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

According to the document, there are five French mother sauces, and the process for making them is as follows:

1. Béchamel (White Sauce):
   a. Make a white roux by melting butter in a saucepan, adding equal parts flour, and cooking for 2-3 minutes while stirring constantly.
   b. Gradually whisk in hot milk.
   c. Simmer until thickened.
   d. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.

2. Velouté:
   a. Make a blonde roux by melting butter in a saucepan, adding equal parts flour, and cooking until light golden (about 5 minutes).
   b. Gradually add hot white stock (chicken, veal, or fish).
   c. Simmer until thickened.
   d. Season to taste.

3. Espagnole (Brown Sauce):
   a. Make a brown roux by melting butter in a saucepan, adding equal parts flour, and cooking until dark brown (about 8-10 minutes).
   b. Add mirepoix and tomato purée.
   c. Gradually incorporate hot brown stock.
   d. Simmer and reduce.
   e. Strain before using.

4. Hollandaise:
   a. Prepare clarified butter.
   b. Create a reduction by combining vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots, reducing by half, then straining and cooling slightly.
   c. Whisk egg yolks with the reduction.
   d. Cook over a double boiler until thickened.
   e. Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter.
   f. Season with lemon juice and cayenne.

5. Tomato Sauce:
   a. Sweat aromatics (onions, carrots, celery, garlic, and herbs).
   b. Add tomatoes and stock.
   c. Simmer until reduced and thickened.
   d. Strain if desired.
   e. Season to taste.

These mother sauces form the basis for many other sauces in French cuisine and are essential components of classical French cooking.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

Hadoop supports secure user impersonation through its Java API. A kerberos-
authenticated user can be allowed to proxy any username that meets specified
criteria entered in the NameNode’s core-site.xml file. This impersonation only
applies to interactions with the Hadoop API or the APIs of Hadoop-related
services that support it (this is not the same as switching to that user on the
machine of origin).
Setting up secure user impersonation (for h2o):
Create or find an id to use as proxy which has limited-to-no access to HDFS
or related services; the proxy user need only be used to impersonate a user (Re-
quired if not using h2odriver) If you are not using the driver (e.g. you wrote your
own code against h2o’s API using Hadoop), make the necessary code changes
to impersonate users (see org.apache.hadoop.security.UserGroupInformation)
In either of Ambari/Cloudera Manager or directly on the NameNode’s core-
site.xml file, add 2/3 properties for the user we wish to use as a proxy (replace

8
To use secure impersonation with h2o’s Hadoop driver:
Before this is attempted, see Risks with impersonation, below
Precautions to take when leveraging secure impersonation The target use
case for secure impersonation is applications or services that pre-authenticate
a user and then use (in this case) the h2odriver on behalf of that user. H2O’s
Steam is a perfect example: auth user in web app over SSL, impersonate that
user when creating the h2o YARN container. The proxy user should have lim-
ited permissions in the Hadoop cluster; this means no permissions to access
data or make API calls. In this way, if it’s compromised it would only have the
power to impersonate a specific subset of the users in the cluster and only from
specific machines. Use the hadoop.proxyuser.¡proxyusername¿.hosts property
whenever possible or practical. Don’t give the proxyusername’s password or
keytab to any user you don’t want to impersonate another user (this is gener-
ally any user). The point of impersonation is not to allow users to impersonate
each other. See the first bullet for the typical use case. Limit user logon to
the machine the proxying is occurring from whenever practical.

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

According to the information provided in the document text, to make hollandaise sauce, follow these steps:

1. **Prepare clarified butter:**
   - Clarify the butter by melting it and separating the milk solids from the fat.

2. **Create the reduction:**
   - Combine vinegar, peppercorns, and shallots in a saucepan.
   - Reduce the mixture by half.
   - Strain the reduction and let it cool slightly.

3. **Whisk egg yolks with reduction:**
   - In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks together with the cooled reduction.

4. **Cook over double boiler:**
   - Place the bowl over a double boiler and cook, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens.

5. **Slowly incorporate warm clarified butter:**
   - Gradually add the warm clarified butter to the egg yolk mixture while continuing to whisk until the sauce is smooth and emulsified.

6. **Season:**
   - Season the hollandaise sauce with lemon juice and cayenne pepper to taste.

typesetting program for formatting its output, and is itself written in the TeX

LaTeX can be used as a standalone document preparation system, or as an
intermediate format. In the latter role, for example, it is sometimes used as part
of a pipeline for translating DocBook and other XML-based formats for PDF.
The typesetting system offers programmable desktop publishing features and
extensive facilities for automating most aspects of typesetting and desktop pub-
lishing, including numbering and cross-referencing of tables and figures, chapter
and section headings, graphics, page layout, indexing and bibliographies.
Like TeX, LaTeX started as a writing tool for mathematicians and computer
scientists, but even from early in its development, it has also been taken up by
scholars who needed to write documents that include complex math expressions
or non-Latin scripts,[7][8] such as Arabic, Devanagari and Chinese.[9]
LaTeX is intended to provide a high-level, descriptive markup language to
utilize TeX more easily. TeX handles the document layout, while LaTeX handles
the content side for document processing. LaTeX comprises a collection of TeX
macros and a program to process LaTeX documents, and because the plain
TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made
commands for formatting and layout requirements such as chapter headings,
footnotes, cross-references and bibliographies.
To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-

style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

LaTeX is intended to provide a high-level, descriptive markup language to
utilize TeX more easily. TeX handles the document layout, while LaTeX handles
the content side for document processing. LaTeX comprises a collection of TeX
macros and a program to process LaTeX documents, and because the plain
TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made
commands for formatting and layout requirements such as chapter headings,

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

intermediate format. In the latter role, for example, it is sometimes used as part
of a pipeline for translating DocBook and other XML-based formats for PDF.
The typesetting system offers programmable desktop publishing features and
extensive facilities for automating most aspects of typesetting and desktop pub-
lishing, including numbering and cross-referencing of tables and figures, chapter
and section headings, graphics, page layout, indexing and bibliographies.
Like TeX, LaTeX started as a writing tool for mathematicians and computer
scientists, but even from early in its development, it has also been taken up by
scholars who needed to write documents that include complex math expressions
or non-Latin scripts,[7][8] such as Arabic, Devanagari and Chinese.[9]
LaTeX is intended to provide a high-level, descriptive markup language to
utilize TeX more easily. TeX handles the document layout, while LaTeX handles
the content side for document processing. LaTeX comprises a collection of TeX
macros and a program to process LaTeX documents, and because the plain
TeX formatting commands are elementary, it provides authors with ready-made
commands for formatting and layout requirements such as chapter headings,
footnotes, cross-references and bibliographies.

to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

To create a document in LaTeX, a user first creates a file, such as doc-
ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-

ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
single window.[20]

ument.tex, typically using a text editor.[15] The user then gives their docu-
ment.tex file as input to the TeX program (with the LaTeX macros loaded),
which prompts TeX to write out a file suitable for onscreen viewing or print-
ing.[16] This write-format-preview cycle is one of the chief ways in which work-
ing with LaTeX differs from the What-You-See-Is-What-You-Get (WYSIWYG)
style of document editing. It is similar to the code-compile-execute cycle known
to computer programmers. Today, many LaTeX-aware editing programs make
this cycle a simple matter through the pressing of a single key, while showing the
output preview on the screen beside the input window. Some online LaTeX ed-
itors even automatically refresh the preview,[17][18][19] while other online tools
provide incremental editing in-place, mixed in with the preview in a streamlined
